capabilities.target: ERP vendor master including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The design relies on a one line approval summary for sensitive bank changes and payments instead of exposing the raw action details to the approver.

elements.name: Scheduled payment instruction to ERP payment process

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only the model generated one line summary, not the raw bank account details or change history. A more capable model can frame or omit critical details more persuasively, and the high approval volume increases consent fatigue.

controls.name: Raw action approval with full bank details and destination payment data shown to clerk
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended replacement for summary only approval so the reviewer sees the actual ERP write and payment destination rather than the model's framing.

controls.name: Scoped ERP credentials limited to approved vendor and payment actions
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended least privilege credentialing so the agent cannot update any vendor or schedule any payment outside an approved scope.

controls.name: Destination account and payee binding to system of record in approval flow
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended control to bind payment destination and bank change target to authoritative ERP records and expose them in the approval workflow.

controls.name: Tamper evident attributable log of agent proposed and approved ERP changes
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended audit record that preserves who approved which raw action and what bank details and payment destination were shown.

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible action (TC9): untrusted invoice can drive broad credential payment scheduling and bank changes through a model-summary approval gate

attack_path.note: Supplier provided invoice can include attacker chosen bank details.
Agent reads confidential vendor master including bank details to match and compare.
Agent can update vendor bank details for any vendor using broad ERP credentials.
Approval gate shows only a one line model summary.
Agent can schedule an irreversible payment using broad ERP credentials.

evidence.observation: The prompt directs the agent to process supplier invoices, update vendor bank details when the invoice shows new bank details, and schedule payment.
The clerk sees only a one line summary: "Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)."
The card shows only the model's summary; bank account numbers and change history are not shown.
The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, which is high approval volume and increases approval fatigue.
The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment, so the agent acts with broader authority than the supplier input source.

recommendations.action: Replace the summary-only approval card with raw action review that shows vendor identity, existing and proposed bank account details, payment destination, amount, and change history before approval.
Reduce ERP credential scope so the agent cannot update arbitrary vendors or schedule arbitrary payments without separate authorization binding.
Bind the approval destination to authoritative ERP vendor records and require explicit confirmation when a bank detail change and a payment are requested in the same workflow.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version changes without review, approval gate is removed or narrowed, or unattended execution increases; the current platform already upgrades the model without separate review.

findings.title: Missing property: approval record is not attributable to the raw ERP action for bank changes and payments

evidence.observation: The approval card records only a one line summary of the action, not the raw bank details or full payment destination.
Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown to the clerk, so the approval record does not fully evidence what was reviewed.

recommendations.action: Create a tamper evident approval record that binds the approver, the exact ERP action, prior and proposed bank details, payment destination, and timestamp.

forecast.watch_signal: No current control restores attributable raw-action provenance; reassess if approval workflow or logging changes.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no inbound identity assertion or peer impersonation path for the subject agent itself.
The artifacts do not show self-configuration, prompt editing, or mutable tool definitions for this agent design.
No explicit external data egress capability beyond payment execution is declared in the reviewed design artifacts.
The reviewed design has no unbounded loop, recursive delegation, or spend-volume abuse evidence beyond the payment path already captured elsewhere.
The artifacts do not say how supplier identities are authenticated in the portal or whether invoice submitters are verified.
The artifacts do not say whether supplier submissions are logged with non-repudiable identity and submission metadata.
The artifacts do not describe transport protections, storage handling, or whether uploaded invoices expose other suppliers' data.
The artifacts do not say whether upload rate controls or queue protections exist for supplier invoice intake.
This boundary flow is used to execute payment instructions rather than disclose confidential data to an external reader in the reviewed design.
The artifacts do not say whether payment scheduling throughput, rate caps, or duplicate submission protections exist.
The artifacts do not say whether the approval record is tamper evident or immutable after clerk action.
The described issue is lack of raw-action detail, not unauthorized disclosure from the approval record store itself.
No availability dependency or attack on the approval record store is evidenced in the supplied artifacts.

rating.rationale: The dominant present risk is an untrusted supplier invoice driving bank-detail changes and irreversible payment scheduling through broad ERP credentials. The only declared preventive control is a human approval gate that shows a model summary rather than the raw action and operates at high volume, so under rubric step 2 it reduces critical inherent risk by one tier to high and cannot reduce below moderate in any case. Forecast rises back to critical if model upgrades continue without review or if autonomy increases, because the summary-based approval gate is partially dependent and explicitly vulnerable to consent-fatigue and framing decay.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt, approval card, and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No ERP schema, supplier portal authentication design, or logging/audit implementation artifacts were provided, so identity verification, duplicate-payment protections, and provenance controls could not be fully assessed.
No source code or runtime traces were provided, so the exact sequencing between vendor read, bank update, and payment scheduling is taken from the prompt and notes.
